requirements.evidence: Every requirement and contract item is in the diff. Migration with cascade FK, nullable invited_by, role default 'employee' and unique (entity_id, email): database/migrations/2026_10_29_062759_create_entity_invites_table.php:16-27. The email Attribute mutator lowercases and trims on every write (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:40-45). Pending/notPending scopes and the 7-day expiry are there. sendInvite trims and validates, checks the rate limit, then calls InviteMember, which rejects existing members (case-insensitive) and pending invites on inviteEmail, replaces expired or accepted rows, and catches UniqueConstraintViolationException (app/Actions/InviteMember.php:43-67). The quota is consumed only after a successful invite (Members.php RateLimiter::hit after handle). PendingInvites accept/decline: 403 for non-invitees, expiry error on 'invite', already accepted is a no-op, firstOrCreate prevents duplicate memberships, and accept sets the session and redirects. The list is rendered on the switcher and on onboarding with a conditional <hr> (pending-invites.blade.php:4-5). The mail is queued markdown with route('login') and all strings in pt_BR.json. Members page: mount authorizes 'update'; openMember uses findOrFail scoped to the entity; the modal title is ui.members_details; the role select has no empty option; saveRole validates, rejects the owner membership and blocks demoting the last manager; the confirmation modal replaces wire:confirm; removeMember resets state.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through new Actions (InviteMember, AcceptInvite, CancelInvite, DeclineInvite), each authorizing via Gate::forUser. EntityInvitePolicy is added. $fillable is set explicitly with the #[Fillable] attribute. The migration has a down() and a generated-style timestamp. CHANGELOG, docs/business-rules.md and docs/database-schema.md are updated. Two small deviations: memberRole is validated inline with $this->validate(['memberRole' => ...]) instead of #[Validate] (Members.php saveRole), and removeMember/saveRole still change memberships directly in the component rather than through Actions (this matches the existing code).

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes on the server: sendInvite, cancelInvite (scoped with $this->entity->invites()->findOrFail), openMember, saveRole (authorize 'assignRole' on a membership scoped to the entity), confirmRemoval, accept/decline (policy checks the invitee's e-mail). Inputs are validated, output uses {{ }} escaping and the rate limit is applied. Remaining gaps: selectedMembershipId is client-writable and not #[Locked], although it is always resolved inside the entity and authorized. Invite acceptance matches only on the e-mail string and never checks that the user's e-mail is verified (the task asks only for an e-mail match).

tests.evidence: Thorough new tests: schema (EntityInviteSchemaTest), model/scopes/normalization (EntityInviteModelTest), mail in both locales (EntityInviteMailTest), actions including the unique-constraint race via a subclass (InviteActionsTest), the Members component (access 403, validation, duplicate member and pending invite, expired replacement, rate-limit quota excluding invalid input, foreign membership not found, draft role, owner tamper, last manager), and PendingInvites (tamper accept/decline, expired, idempotent, redirect/session). Weakness: the 'employees cannot send, cancel or change anything' test calls cancelInvite/removeMember on a component whose mount already returns 403, so those calls never reach the methods and do not test their own authorization.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall, and it reuses existing policies ('update' on Entity, 'assignRole' on membership) and the existing removal rules. There is some redundancy: PendingInvites::accept/decline call $this->authorize and then the Action authorizes again through Gate. InviteMember lowercases the e-mail by hand even though the model mutator and forEmail scope already normalize it. isPending() is only used in tests.

readability.evidence: Methods are short, focused and documented with PHPDoc (e.g. Members::saveRole, InviteMember::handle). Names are clear (INVITES_PER_HOUR, inviteRateKey, hasPendingInvite). Comments explain non-obvious choices such as the row lock in AcceptInvite and the race in InviteMember. Blade follows the Bulma modal-card patterns, and I found no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. The navbar and dashboard edits (layouts/default-page.blade.php:44, dashboard.blade.php) follow from the members page becoming manager-only. The extra invite deletion when an entity is soft-deleted (Settings.php:84) is not requested, but it is small, related, tested and in the changelog.

issues.location: tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php ('employees cannot send, cancel or change anything')
issues.explanation: Mount already returns 403 for employees, so the cancelInvite/removeMember calls never run and the test does not show that those methods authorize on their own.

Acceptance relies only on a string match with the account's e-mail and does not require it to be verified, so someone who registers an unverified account with the invited address could accept the invite.
This server-context ID is client-writable rather than #[Locked]; the risk is limited because saveRole re-resolves it inside the entity and authorizes it.
memberRole is validated inline instead of with the #[Validate] attribute the project uses for public properties.
The component authorizes accept/decline and then the Action authorizes the same ability again.
Deleting invites on entity soft-delete was not requested, though it is a small related safeguard and it is tested.

review.summary: The change replaces instant member addition with an invite flow: a new table, model, factory and policy, four Actions, a queued markdown mail, a PendingInvites component on onboarding and the switcher, and a manager-only members page with a details modal, an explicit save-role button and a removal confirmation modal. It meets every requirement, including the race and quota edge cases, follows the Action/policy conventions, updates the docs and ships comprehensive tests. Only minor issues remain: one test that cannot reach the methods it means to check, an unlocked selection ID, and some redundant authorization.
